Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Bristle toothbrush (China): Chinese records show a Hongzhi emperor using boar bristles set into bone or bamboo, and Europeans later imported the idea.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Mum deodorant: Mum, patented in Philadelphia, was a zinc-based cream that people applied by finger, widely seen as the first commercial deodorant.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Toothpaste in a tube: Dr Washington Sheffield of Connecticut sold toothpaste in collapsible tubes, inspired by the tubes artists used for paint.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Gillette safety razor: King Camp Gillette's idea was to sell the razor cheaply and make money on disposable blades, a model still copied today.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Kleenex tissues: Kleenex began as a cold-cream remover, until customers started using it to blow their noses, so the company changed the marketing.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Tampax tampons: Doctor Earle Haas patented the applicator tampon, and Gertrude Tenderich bought the patent and made early ones at home.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Electric toothbrush: Introduced in Switzerland, early electric toothbrushes were designed for patients with limited dexterity.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Pampers diapers: Victor Mills, a Procter and Gamble engineer, designed these disposable diapers, reportedly motivated by cloth diapers on his grandchild.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Home pregnancy test: The first one, e.p.t., took about two hours and needed a test tube, a dropper and a mirror to read.
Everyday hygiene and health products, by.Fitbit tracker: The clip-on tracker launched the wearable fitness craze, and Google bought the company in 2021 for about 2.1 billion dollars.

Saints' feast days through the year.St Agnes: The Roman martyr Agnes is the patron of girls. John Keats set a poem on the night before her day, 'The Eve of St Agnes'.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Blaise: Blaise's day brings the blessing of throats with two crossed candles, after a legend that he saved a boy choking on a fish bone.
Saints' feast days through the year.St David: The patron saint of Wales, David is honored on this day with daffodils and leeks, and Welsh children often wear traditional dress.
Saints' feast days through the year.St George: England's patron saint shares his day with the traditional date of Shakespeare's birth. His dragon-slaying legend was added in the Middle Ages.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Joan of Arc: The day marks the date Joan was burned at the stake in Rouen in 1431. She was declared a saint nearly 500 years later, in 1920.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Swithun: English weather lore says that if it rains on Swithun's day, it will rain for forty more days. If it is dry, forty dry ones follow.
Saints' feast days through the year.St James the Great: The patron saint of pilgrims, this apostle's shrine at Santiago de Compostela is the end of the Camino. The scallop shell is his emblem.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Francis of Assisi: Patron of animals and ecology, Francis gave away his father's goods and chose poverty. World Animal Day is held on this date.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Luke: Tradition names Luke as the author of a Gospel and the Acts, and as a physician. He is the patron saint of artists.
Saints' feast days through the year.St Lucy: Her name comes from the Latin for light, and on her day Swedish girls in white robes wear candle crowns in the Lucia procession.

How much these giants weigh.Wright Flyer: The 1903 plane's first flight lasted 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk, and it steered by warping its wings with cables instead of using flaps.
How much these giants weigh.Ford Model T: Ford used lightweight, strong vanadium steel, which helped keep this cheap car light enough to survive rutted rural roads.
How much these giants weigh.Space Shuttle orbiter (empty): Its body was covered by over 20,000 heat-shield tiles, each fitted individually to protect against re-entry temperatures.
How much these giants weigh.Statue of Liberty: Its copper skin is only about 2.4 mm thick, and the green colour is natural oxidation. Gustave Eiffel designed the iron frame inside.
How much these giants weigh.Big Boy locomotive + tender: Union Pacific built just 25 of these giant 4-8-8-4 locomotives from 1941 to haul freight over Wyoming's mountains. Eight survive.
How much these giants weigh.An-225 at max takeoff: Its Ukrainian name Mriya means 'dream'. Only one was ever completed, and it was destroyed at Hostomel airfield in 2022.
How much these giants weigh.Saturn V, fueled: At 110 m tall it is still the most powerful rocket to fly successfully, and it carried every Apollo crew to the Moon.
How much these giants weigh.Eiffel Tower: Built for the 1889 World's Fair and meant to stand just 20 years, its iron is repainted roughly every seven years.
How much these giants weigh.RMS Titanic: This is its displacement, not its registered tonnage. She had lifeboats for only about half the 2,200 people aboard when she sank in 1912.
How much these giants weigh.Seawise Giant, fully laden: A supertanker over 450 m long, longer than the Empire State Building is tall. Damaged in the Iran-Iraq war, it was raised and sailed again.

Boiling points of household liquids.Liquid nitrogen: So cold it freezes things brittle on contact, and it's used by doctors to remove warts.
Boiling points of household liquids.Propane: Stored as a liquid under pressure in tanks, at normal pressure it would boil away at this chilly temperature.
Boiling points of household liquids.Butane (lighter fuel): Lighter fuel is liquid under pressure but boils near freezing, so cheap lighters struggle on cold days.
Boiling points of household liquids.Acetone (nail polish remover): It dissolves nail polish, evaporates fast, and is highly flammable.
Boiling points of household liquids.Ethanol: Ethanol boils lower than water, which is exactly why distillation can concentrate alcohol.
Boiling points of household liquids.Isopropyl rubbing alcohol: Rubbing alcohol is usually about 70 percent, since the water helps it kill germs better than pure alcohol.
Boiling points of household liquids.Water: Water boils at 100 °C only at sea level, and on Everest it boils at around 70 °C.
Boiling points of household liquids.Antifreeze (ethylene glycol): Ethylene glycol is sweet but toxic, and its high boiling point helps it protect engines.
Boiling points of household liquids.Glycerin: Thick and sweet-tasting, glycerin is used in soaps, food and e-cigarette liquids.
Boiling points of household liquids.Mercury: The only common metal liquid at room temperature, and it was long used in thermometers until phased out.

Czech month names, in calendar order.leden: Czech's word for January comes from led, meaning ice, and unlike English it is a native word, not borrowed from Latin like January.
Czech month names, in calendar order.únor: Its name is tied to an old verb for submerging, probably describing ice sinking and breaking up as winter loosens its grip.
Czech month names, in calendar order.duben: Its name comes from dub, oak, since oaks come into leaf around then; Czech month names mostly describe what nature is doing.
Czech month names, in calendar order.květen: It comes from květ, blossom, because fruit trees bloom then; a flower is květina, so the connection is easy to remember.
Czech month names, in calendar order.červen: Czech has červen for June and červenec for July, differing by one suffix, which easily confuses learners; both are linked to the color red.
Czech month names, in calendar order.červenec: Often mixed up with its neighbor červen, this is July; both names are tied to red, perhaps from ripening fruit or the dye cochineal.
Czech month names, in calendar order.srpen: It comes from srp, a sickle, the tool for the harvest, and Czech uses this farmer's word where English uses Latin Augustus.
Czech month names, in calendar order.září: Unlike English September, it is a native Czech name, and it echoes záře, glow, though scholars have argued about its exact origin.
Czech month names, in calendar order.listopad: The name means leaf-fall, from list, leaf, and padat, to fall; a vivid autumn picture that the Latin-based English months lack.
Czech month names, in calendar order.prosinec: Its exact origin is debated, with one theory tying it to the pale, thin light of midwinter, and another to an old word for asking.

How the World Wide Web grew up.Berners-Lee's web proposal: Tim Berners-Lee wrote it at CERN, where his boss reportedly scribbled 'Vague but exciting' on it.
How the World Wide Web grew up.First US web server: This server was set up at SLAC in California in December 1991.
How the World Wide Web grew up.CERN frees the web: On 30 April 1993, CERN placed the web software in the public domain.
How the World Wide Web grew up.W3C founded: Berners-Lee founded this at MIT to set web standards.
How the World Wide Web grew up.Netscape IPO: Shares doubled on the first day, kicking off the dot-com boom.
How the World Wide Web grew up.CSS level 1: This separated a page's style from its content; it was created by Hakon Wium Lie and Bert Bos.
How the World Wide Web grew up.Dot-com bubble peaks: The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000 around 5,000 and then fell about 78 percent.
How the World Wide Web grew up.First Web 2.0 conference: Tim O'Reilly's conference popularised the term for user-generated, interactive sites.
How the World Wide Web grew up.HTML5 finalized: It brought native video and audio, ending the need for Flash plugins.
How the World Wide Web grew up.HTTP/2 standardized: It lets multiple requests share one connection, speeding up pages; it grew from Google's SPDY.

Recent and future Summer Olympics.Atlanta: The Centennial Games took place in Coca-Cola's hometown, and a bomb went off in a park during them, killing one person.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Sydney: Cathy Freeman, an Indigenous Australian sprinter, lit the cauldron and later won the 400 metres gold.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Athens (second time): It returned the Games to their birthplace, and the marathon followed the route from Marathon to Athens.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Beijing Summer Games: It opened at 8:08 pm on 8/8/08, in the Bird's Nest stadium, because 8 is a lucky number in China.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.London (third time): It was the first city to host the Summer Games three times: 1908, 1948 and 2012.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Rio de Janeiro: The first Games held in South America, where the opening ceremony took place in Maracana stadium.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Tokyo (second time): The Games were postponed a year by the pandemic and held mostly without spectators, but kept the original name.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Paris (third time): Its opening ceremony was held on the Seine rather than in a stadium, and it was the city's third Games, after 1900 and 1924.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Los Angeles (third time): It will join Paris and London in hosting three times, after hosting in 1932 and 1984.
Recent and future Summer Olympics.Brisbane: It will be the third Australian city to host, after Melbourne in 1956 and Sydney in 2000.

Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Men's high jump: Javier Sotomayor of Cuba cleared it in 1993, and no one has topped it in over three decades.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Women's long jump: Galina Chistyakova of the Soviet Union jumped it in 1988, and the mark has stood for decades.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Men's long jump: Mike Powell's leap in Tokyo in 1991 beat Bob Beamon's 1968 mark, set in thin high-altitude air in Mexico City.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Men's triple jump: Jonathan Edwards of Britain set it in Gothenburg in 1995, becoming the first man to triple jump over 18 meters.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Women's shot put: Natalya Lisovskaya threw it in 1987, and it has stood for more than 35 years.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Women's javelin: Barbora Spotakova of the Czech Republic set it in 2008 and has won two Olympic golds.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Women's discus: Gabriele Reinsch of East Germany threw it in 1988, and it is among the oldest records in athletics.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Women's hammer: Anita Wlodarczyk of Poland threw it in 2016, the first woman past 80 meters, and won three Olympic titles.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Men's hammer: Yuriy Sedykh set it in 1986 and remains the champion's mark; he also won two Olympic golds.
Long-standing jump and throw world recor.Men's javelin: Jan Zelezny of the Czech Republic set it in 1996, using a javelin redesigned after 1986 to land sooner and reduce dangerous throws.

Wizarding World films in story order.Fantastic Beasts: Newt Scamander's book is also a real one: Rowling published it in 2001 as a Hogwarts textbook, with sales raising money for charity.
Wizarding World films in story order.The Crimes of Grindelwald: Much of it is set in Paris, including a scene at the Père Lachaise cemetery.
Wizarding World films in story order.The Secrets of Dumbledore: Mads Mikkelsen replaced Johnny Depp as Grindelwald for this third installment.
Wizarding World films in story order.Philosopher's Stone: It was retitled Sorcerer's Stone in the US because the publisher thought philosopher sounded less magical.
Wizarding World films in story order.Chamber of Secrets: It introduced Dobby, a house-elf made with computer animation who became one of the series' favorite characters.
Wizarding World films in story order.Prisoner of Azkaban: Alfonso Cuarón directed it and gave the series a darker, more visual tone, introducing the Time-Turner.
Wizarding World films in story order.Goblet of Fire: It was the first Potter film rated PG-13 in the US and features the Triwizard Tournament.
Wizarding World films in story order.Order of the Phoenix: David Yates directed it and then stayed to direct every remaining film in the series.
Wizarding World films in story order.Half-Blood Prince: It earned an Oscar nomination for its cinematography, which was done by Bruno Delbonnel.
Wizarding World films in story order.Deathly Hallows Part 2: As the final film, it earned over $1.3 billion worldwide, making it the series' biggest hit.

Music biopics by release.Coal Miner's Daughter: Sissy Spacek won the Best Actress Oscar playing Loretta Lynn, and she sang the songs herself.
Music biopics by release.Amadeus: It won eight Oscars including Best Picture; the rivalry between Salieri and Mozart is largely fiction.
Music biopics by release.La Bamba: Ritchie Valens died at 17 in the 1959 plane crash that also killed Buddy Holly; Los Lobos recorded the soundtrack.
Music biopics by release.The Doors: Val Kilmer sang the songs himself, in Oliver Stone's film about Jim Morrison.
Music biopics by release.What's Love Got to Do with It: Angela Bassett earned an Oscar nomination for playing Tina Turner, depicting her abusive marriage to Ike.
Music biopics by release.Ray: Jamie Foxx won the Best Actor Oscar for playing Ray Charles, who died shortly before the film's release.
Music biopics by release.Walk the Line: Reese Witherspoon won Best Actress as June Carter, and Joaquin Phoenix sang as Johnny Cash.
Music biopics by release.Bohemian Rhapsody: Rami Malek won Best Actor as Freddie Mercury, and it became the highest-grossing music biopic.
Music biopics by release.Elvis: Baz Luhrmann directed it, with Austin Butler as the King and Tom Hanks as Colonel Tom Parker.
Music biopics by release.A Complete Unknown: Timothée Chalamet plays the young Bob Dylan, including the controversial 1965 Newport Folk Festival electric set.

Flat things by area.US postage stamp: The Penny Black of 1840 was the world's first adhesive postage stamp, issued in Britain.
Flat things by area.Credit card: Cards follow the ISO ID-1 standard at 85.6 by 54 mm, the same size as driver's licenses and bank cards worldwide.
Flat things by area.A4 sheet: Its sides are in the ratio 1 to the square root of 2, so folding a sheet in half keeps the same proportions.
Flat things by area.Standard door: US accessibility rules require at least 32 inches of clear width for a wheelchair to pass through a doorway.
Flat things by area.King-size bed: A California king is narrower and longer than a standard king.
Flat things by area.Parking space: Stalls were drawn for the cars of earlier decades, and as vehicles have grown, many feel tight.
Flat things by area.Tennis court: Singles are played on a narrower court than doubles: the doubles court is 78 feet by 36 feet.
Flat things by area.NBA basketball court: It is 94 by 50 feet. FIBA's international courts are a bit smaller at 28 by 15 meters.
Flat things by area.Olympic pool surface: The standard pool is 50 by 25 meters with 2.5-meter lanes and holds about 2.5 million liters of water.
Flat things by area.Soccer pitch: A typical pitch is 105 by 68 meters, though the rules allow some variation.

Constellations by area of sky.Crux (Southern Cross): The smallest of all 88 constellations, it has four bright stars and appears on the flags of Australia and New Zealand.
Constellations by area of sky.Canis Minor: Its star Procyon is among the nearest bright stars, and the Little Dog follows Orion.
Constellations by area of sky.Lyra: It holds Vega, one of the sky's brightest stars, and the Ring Nebula.
Constellations by area of sky.Scorpius: The hooked tail looks like what it is named for, which is unusual.
Constellations by area of sky.Orion: The Orion Nebula, visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy patch, is a stellar nursery.
Constellations by area of sky.Cygnus: Shaped like the Northern Cross, it contains Deneb, and the Kepler telescope stared at its field to find planets.
Constellations by area of sky.Leo: Its stars form a backward question mark known as the Sickle, the lion's head and mane.
Constellations by area of sky.Pegasus: The Great Square of Pegasus is a handy guide for finding the Andromeda Galaxy.
Constellations by area of sky.Hercules: Though faint, it hosts M13, a globular cluster of hundreds of thousands of stars.
Constellations by area of sky.Hydra: The largest of all constellations, stretching across a quarter of the sky around.

When these odd buildings went up.Leaning Tower of Pisa (begun): It began leaning while still being built because of soft ground on one side, and the tilt was reduced in the 1990s.
When these odd buildings went up.Palais Idéal du Facteur Cheval: A postman named Ferdinand Cheval built it by hand from stones he collected on his rounds, over some 33 years.
When these odd buildings went up.Lucy the Elephant: The six-storey wooden elephant in New Jersey was built to promote real-estate sales, and has also served as a home and a tavern.
When these odd buildings went up.Winchester Mystery House: Sarah Winchester's mansion in San Jose, with its stairs to nowhere, was built nonstop for decades.
When these odd buildings went up.Watts Towers: Italian immigrant Simon Rodia built these spires alone over 33 years, from steel rods, scrap and broken tile.
When these odd buildings went up.The Big Duck: Built on Long Island to sell ducks, it inspired architect Robert Venturi to call buildings shaped like their purpose 'ducks'.
When these odd buildings went up.Haines Shoe House: Built by 'the Shoe Wizard' Mahlon Haines as an advertisement for his shoe business, it was later rented to honeymooning couples.
When these odd buildings went up.Atomium: The 102-metre model of an iron crystal, enlarged some 165 billion times, was built for the Brussels World's Fair of 1958.
When these odd buildings went up.Dancing House (Prague): Nicknamed 'Fred and Ginger' for its pair of towers that seem to dance, it was designed by Vlado Milunic with Frank Gehry.
When these odd buildings went up.Longaberger Basket Building: A seven-storey office shaped like a giant picnic basket, it was the head office of a basket company in Newark, Ohio.

F1 champions, by first title.Juan Manuel Fangio: The Argentine won five titles in the 1950s, with four different teams, and in 1958 was kidnapped by Cuban rebels before a race.
F1 champions, by first title.Jim Clark: The Scottish farmer's son won two titles and also the 1965 Indianapolis 500, and died in a Formula 2 race in 1968.
F1 champions, by first title.Jackie Stewart: After a crash at Spa in 1966 he pushed for safety, popularising full-face helmets and seat belts, and won three titles.
F1 champions, by first title.Niki Lauda: He returned to racing just six weeks after a fiery crash at the Nürburgring in 1976, and won two more titles later.
F1 champions, by first title.Alain Prost: Nicknamed 'The Professor' for his cerebral driving, he won four titles and had a famously bitter rivalry with Senna.
F1 champions, by first title.Ayrton Senna: The Brazilian won three titles, and his death at Imola in 1994 led to sweeping safety reforms and a national mourning.
F1 champions, by first title.Michael Schumacher: He won seven titles, a record he shares with Hamilton, including five in a row for Ferrari from 2000 to 2004.
F1 champions, by first title.Fernando Alonso: At 24 he was the youngest champion to that date, and he ended Schumacher's reign with Renault, then won again in 2006.
F1 champions, by first title.Lewis Hamilton: He won his first title on the final corner of the last race in 2008, and became the first Black champion in F1.
F1 champions, by first title.Max Verstappen: He clinched it on the last lap of the final race in Abu Dhabi, after a controversial safety car, having been the youngest ever race winner at 18.

Pokémon game releases (Japan).Red and Green: Pokémon began as two Game Boy games in Japan in February 1996. Creator Satoshi Tajiri based it on his childhood love of collecting insects.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Yellow: The 1998 version let Pikachu follow the player around, and matched the hit anime, in which Ash's Pikachu refuses to stay in its Poké Ball.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Gold and Silver: Johto's debut added 100 new Pokémon, plus day and night cycles and a clock that ran in real time, and the ability to link to the originals.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Ruby and Sapphire: The first Game Boy Advance generation, set in Hoenn, introduced abilities, weather effects and double battles to the main games.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Diamond and Pearl: Released for the Nintendo DS in 2006, and notable for its online trading and battling over Wi-Fi, a first for the series.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Black and White: Set in Unova, a region modeled on New York, these DS games used only brand-new Pokémon until the postgame and added triple battles.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).X and Y: The first mainline games to be released worldwide on the same day, in 3D on the Nintendo 3DS, and introduced Mega Evolution.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Sun and Moon: Set in Alola, a Hawaii-inspired region, they dropped the usual gym badges and used island trials instead.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Sword and Shield: The first mainline games for the Nintendo Switch, set in a region modeled on Britain, with giant Dynamax battles.
Pokémon game releases (Japan).Scarlet and Violet: The first fully open-world Pokémon games, set in Paldea, a region inspired by Spain and Portugal, and let players explore in any order.

How tall these skyscrapers stand.Chrysler Building: The Chrysler Building was briefly the world's tallest, and its steel spire was assembled secretly inside the building then raised.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Empire State Building: The Empire State Building was built in just over a year, and it was the world's tallest for about 40 years.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Petronas Towers: The Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world in the late 1990s, and they are joined by a skybridge.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Taipei 101: Taipei 101 was once the world's tallest, and it holds a giant damper ball to calm sway in typhoons.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.One World Trade Center: One World Trade Center's height of 1,776 feet nods to the year of American independence.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Lotte World Tower, Seoul: Lotte World Tower is the tallest in South Korea, and it has a glass-floored observation deck high above Seoul.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower: The Abraj Al-Bait clock tower in Mecca has one of the largest clock faces in the world.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Shanghai Tower: Shanghai Tower twists as it rises to reduce wind forces, and it's the tallest in China.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Merdeka 118, Kuala Lumpur: Merdeka 118 is Malaysia's tallest, and its crown design is inspired by the raised fist of independence.
How tall these skyscrapers stand.Burj Khalifa, Dubai: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world, and its top is so high that residents see the sun set twice.

When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of the Franks: Clovis, its famous king, converted to Catholic Christianity, and his realm became the seed of both France and Germany.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Asturias: Tradition says Pelagius defeated a Muslim force at Covadonga and began this kingdom, the starting point of the Reconquista.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Alba (Scotland): Kenneth MacAlpin is credited with uniting Picts and Scots, founding the kingdom that became Scotland.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of England: Athelstan became the first king to rule all of England after he took York from the Vikings.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Hungary: Stephen I was crowned around this year and later made a saint; he turned a tribal people into a Christian kingdom.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Poland: Boleslaw the Brave was crowned king just before he died, making Poland a recognised kingdom.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Jerusalem: Founded after the First Crusade; its first ruler, Godfrey of Bouillon, refused a royal crown where Christ wore thorns.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Sicily: Roger II's Norman kingdom blended Norman, Arab and Byzantine culture, with a glittering court in Palermo.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Kingdom of Bohemia: Its kings got a hereditary crown; Prague later became capital of the Holy Roman Empire under Charles IV.
When these medieval kingdoms were born.Nasrid Kingdom of Granada: The last Muslim state in Iberia, it built the Alhambra and survived until 1492, when Granada fell to Castile and Aragon.

How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Daft Punk: The French duo, famous for their robot helmets, split in 2021.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.The Police: Sting, Stewart Copeland and Andy Summers made Synchronicity in 1983.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.The Beatles: They played in Hamburg as a five-piece with Stuart Sutcliffe and Pete Best before the lineup changed.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Spice Girls: Their nicknames, Scary, Sporty, Baby, Ginger and Posh, were coined by a magazine.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Volleyball team on court: Players rotate clockwise when they win the serve.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Snow White's dwarfs: Disney named them Doc, Grumpy, Happy, Sleepy, Bashful, Sneezy and Dopey; the Grimms' tale never named them.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Baseball team in the field: Nine players and nine innings: a baseball team fields nine at a time.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Soccer team on the pitch: A match must be abandoned if a team has fewer than seven players.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Jesus's apostles: The number matched the twelve tribes of Israel; Matthias replaced Judas after his betrayal.
How many members? Bands, teams and legen.Rugby union team on field: Rugby league has 13 and sevens has seven; union has the most players on the pitch.

When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Mariner 4: The first successful flyby sent 22 grainy photos showing a cratered surface, to scientists' disappointment.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Mariner 9: The first spacecraft ever to orbit another planet, it arrived just as a global dust storm hid the surface.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Viking 1: It landed on 20 July 1976, the American bicentennial year, and transmitted for over six years.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Mars Pathfinder: It carried Sojourner, the first wheeled rover on Mars, and used a landing system of airbags.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Mars Express: The European Space Agency's first Mars mission mapped water ice, and carried a lander that was lost.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Spirit rover: Designed for just 90 days, the rover kept working for more than six years, long past expectations.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Phoenix lander: It landed near the north pole and dug up water ice, confirming what orbiters had suspected.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Curiosity rover: A car-sized rover lowered by a 'sky crane' after a nail-biting landing sequence nicknamed 'seven minutes of terror'.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.InSight lander: It put the first seismometer on Mars and recorded hundreds of marsquakes before ending in 2022.
When these spacecraft arrived at Mars.Perseverance rover: It carried the Ingenuity helicopter, which made the first powered flight on another planet.

Frequencies from music to light.Lowest piano note: That is A0, a note so deep many small speakers can't reproduce it. It's felt as much as heard.
Frequencies from music to light.European mains electricity: Europe uses 50 Hz, while North America runs on 60 Hz, one reason travel appliances can be fussy.
Frequencies from music to light.Middle C: Called C4, it sits near the centre of the keyboard and is where piano students usually place their right thumb to begin.
Frequencies from music to light.Concert A: Orchestras tune to this note, usually sounded by the oboe. A 1939 conference helped fix 440 Hz as the standard.
Frequencies from music to light.Highest piano note: The top key, C8, is a piercing pitch that only a few instruments, such as the piccolo, can come close to matching.
Frequencies from music to light.Upper limit of human hearing: Hearing at the top end fades with age, and many adults can't detect anything much above 15 to 17 kHz.
Frequencies from music to light.AM radio station: AM stands for amplitude modulation, and the signal bounces off the sky at night, so far-away stations are heard after dark.
Frequencies from music to light.FM radio station: Edwin Armstrong invented frequency modulation to get static-free radio. FM broadcasts sit around 88 to 108 MHz.
Frequencies from music to light.Microwave oven: Contrary to myth, it isn't tuned to water's resonance. 2.45 GHz simply penetrates food well and is allowed for licence-free use.
Frequencies from music to light.Green light: Human eyes are most sensitive to green light, around 555 nanometres, which is why night-vision displays and many lasers use green.

Turning points in the Middle East.Ottomans conquer Egypt: The Ottoman sultan Selim I defeated the Mamluks and took Egypt, and he also took the title of caliph, which later passed to his successors.
Turning points in the Middle East.Napoleon invades Egypt: Napoleon's campaign brought scholars, and the Rosetta Stone was discovered, which later allowed the deciphering of hieroglyphs.
Turning points in the Middle East.Sykes-Picot Agreement: Britain and France secretly planned to divide Ottoman lands, and the straight-line borders are still blamed for later conflicts.
Turning points in the Middle East.Saudi Arabia founded: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud unified the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd, and it was named after his family, and oil was found six years later.
Turning points in the Middle East.Israel founded: David Ben-Gurion declared the state, and neighbouring Arab states attacked the next day, beginning the first Arab-Israeli war.
Turning points in the Middle East.Suez Crisis: Egypt's nationalisation of the canal led to a British, French and Israeli invasion, and U.S. pressure forced them to withdraw.
Turning points in the Middle East.Six-Day War: Israel captured the Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank and the Golan Heights in just six days, changing the region's map.
Turning points in the Middle East.Yom Kippur War: Egypt and Syria attacked on the Jewish holy day, and the Arab oil embargo that followed caused fuel shortages in the West.
Turning points in the Middle East.Gulf War: A U.S.-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait after a short air and ground campaign, called Desert Storm.
Turning points in the Middle East.Oslo Accords: Israeli and Palestinian leaders shook hands on the White House lawn, and the accords created the Palestinian Authority.

Default port numbers of these services.FTP: File Transfer Protocol dates from the early 1970s, which makes it one of the internet's oldest services.
Default port numbers of these services.SSH: Tatu Ylönen created it in 1995 after a password-sniffing attack hit his Finnish university, replacing insecure remote logins.
Default port numbers of these services.SMTP (email sending): Many internet providers block outgoing traffic on this port to stop infected computers from sending spam.
Default port numbers of these services.DNS: This service is the internet's phone book, turning names such as example.com into the numeric addresses computers need.
Default port numbers of these services.HTTP: Tim Berners-Lee's web protocol runs on this port, though browsers hide the ':80' from addresses.
Default port numbers of these services.POP3: The name stands for Post Office Protocol, as mail waits on a server until your program fetches it.
Default port numbers of these services.HTTPS: The padlock in your browser means traffic uses this port, and over 90 percent of page loads in Chrome now do so.
Default port numbers of these services.MySQL: The database is named after My, the daughter of co-founder Monty Widenius.
Default port numbers of these services.PostgreSQL: Its name nods to its ancestor Ingres, as the project began at Berkeley as the successor 'Post-Ingres'.
Default port numbers of these services.Minecraft server: The game has sold over 300 million copies, and each Java server listens here by default, unless its owner changes it.

Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Argand oil lamp: Swiss inventor Aimé Argand's hollow wick let air flow through the flame, producing a much brighter, smokeless light.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Gas lighting (Murdoch): Scottish engineer William Murdoch lit his Cornish home with coal gas, and London streets followed in the next decades.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Kerosene lamp: Polish pharmacist Ignacy Łukasiewicz built the first practical one in Lviv, and cheap kerosene helped ease the demand for whale oil.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Edison's light bulb: Edison tested thousands of filament materials, including bamboo, and Joseph Swan was working on the same idea in England.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Neon sign: Georges Claude showed neon at the Paris Motor Show in 1910, and a barber shop was among its first uses in advertising.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Fluorescent lamp: Fluorescent lamps were launched in 1938 and became popular in offices, because they use much less energy than bulbs.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Halogen lamp: Hotter than ordinary bulbs, it has a quartz glass that mustn't be touched with bare fingers, as the oils can crack it.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Red LED: General Electric's Nick Holonyak invented the first visible-light LED, which was red and was used for indicator lights.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Lava lamp: Edward Craven Walker invented it after seeing an egg timer made from a bottle of liquid in a pub.
Lighting up the dark, oldest to newest.Blue LED: Three Japanese scientists made the bright blue LED possible, which made white LEDs and a 2014 Nobel Prize.

Italian inventions and discoveries.Eyeglasses: A friar's sermon from 1306 says eyeglasses had been invented about twenty years before, probably in northern Italy.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Galileo's telescope: He saw Jupiter's four big moons in 1610, which proved that not everything in the sky circled the Earth.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Torricelli's barometer: Evangelista Torricelli's mercury tube proved that air has weight, and the pressure unit torr is named after him.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Cristofori's piano: Bartolomeo Cristofori called it a harpsichord with soft and loud, which is why we call it piano.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Galvani's frog experiments: Luigi Galvani saw dissected frog legs twitch when touched by metal, which led him to propose animal electricity.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Volta's battery: Alessandro Volta's pile of metal discs gave the first steady electric current, and the volt is named after him.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Espresso machine: Angelo Moriondo of Turin patented a steam machine for making coffee in bulk, years before the modern espresso machine.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Marconi's radio: He sent a signal over about two kilometres in his father's garden, and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Fermi's nuclear reactor: Enrico Fermi's team built Chicago Pile-1 under a football stadium's stands and started the first controlled chain reaction.
Italian inventions and discoveries.Nutella: Pietro Ferrero's family in Alba made hazelnut chocolate paste when cocoa was scarce, and Nutella got its name in 1964.

When these famous roads opened.Appian Way: Called the queen of long roads, it linked Rome to southern Italy; in 71 BC, 6,000 followers of Spartacus were crucified along it.
When these famous roads opened.Lincoln Highway: The first road to cross the US coast to coast, from New York to San Francisco, was planned by private citizens before the government.
When these famous roads opened.AVUS, Berlin: Berlin's AVUS was an early motorway-style road that doubled as a race track, famous for its steeply banked north curve.
When these famous roads opened.Route 66: Called the Mother Road, it ran about 2,400 miles from Chicago to Santa Monica and was decommissioned in 1985 after interstates replaced it.
When these famous roads opened.Great Ocean Road: Built by returned World War I soldiers, this cliff-hugging Australian road is described as the world's largest war memorial.
When these famous roads opened.Pennsylvania Turnpike: It was America's first long-distance superhighway, partly using old railway tunnels, and at first had no speed limit.
When these famous roads opened.Alaska Highway: US Army engineers built it in about eight months after Pearl Harbor, running some 2,200 km from Dawson Creek, British Columbia, to Alaska.
When these famous roads opened.M1 motorway: Britain's first major inter-city motorway opened between London and Birmingham with no speed limit and no crash barriers.
When these famous roads opened.Trans-Canada Highway: About 7,800 km long, it runs across all ten provinces, from Victoria, British Columbia, to St. John's, Newfoundland.
When these famous roads opened.Karakoram Highway: It links Pakistan and China across the Khunjerab Pass, at about 4,700 m, among the highest paved international crossings on Earth.

Ancient lives: who was born first?.Pythagoras: Pythagoras ran a secretive school, and the theorem named for him was known to Babylonians over a thousand years earlier.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Confucius: Confucius's teachings, collected by his disciples in the Analects, shaped Chinese society and government for over 2,000 years.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Socrates: Socrates wrote nothing himself; we know him from Plato and others, and he was sentenced to death by drinking hemlock.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Plato: Plato founded the Academy in Athens, a school that lasted for centuries, and wrote dialogues starring Socrates.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Aristotle: Aristotle tutored a teenage Alexander the Great and founded his own school, the Lyceum, in Athens.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Alexander the Great: Alexander never lost a battle, and built an empire from Greece to India before dying at 32.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Archimedes: Archimedes is said to have shouted Eureka in the bath, and was killed during the Roman siege of Syracuse in 212 BC.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Julius Caesar: As a young man Caesar was kidnapped by pirates, and after his ransom was paid he came back and had them crucified.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Cleopatra: Cleopatra was of Macedonian Greek descent, and was the first of her dynasty to learn the Egyptian language.
Ancient lives: who was born first?.Jesus of Nazareth: The year 1 was set by a monk in the sixth century, but most historians place Jesus's birth a few years earlier, before Herod died in 4 BC.

When these currencies were introduced.US dollar: Created by the Coinage Act, its name comes from the German 'thaler'. Its familiar green notes date to the Civil War.
When these currencies were introduced.Swiss franc: The Swiss federal franc replaced a patchwork of cantonal currencies. Its code is CHF.
When these currencies were introduced.Canadian dollar: Switched to decimal in 1858. Its dollar coin is called the loonie after the bird on it.
When these currencies were introduced.Japanese yen: Introduced under the Meiji government. 'Yen' means round object.
When these currencies were introduced.Reichsmark: Replaced the hyperinflated paper mark that had become nearly worthless.
When these currencies were introduced.Deutsche Mark: Introduced in the western occupation zones in 1948, and a sign of Germany's postwar recovery.
When these currencies were introduced.South African rand: Launched when South Africa became a republic in 1961, and named for the Witwatersrand gold fields.
When these currencies were introduced.Australian dollar: Replaced the pound in 1966. Names considered included the 'royal' and the 'austral'.
When these currencies were introduced.UK decimal coinage: Decimal Day, 15 February 1971, swapped 240 old pence per pound for 100 new pence.
When these currencies were introduced.Euro notes and coins: Notes and coins entered circulation in 2002 in twelve countries, replacing national currencies.

African countries by population.Seychelles: The smallest African country by population is spread over about 115 islands and grows the giant coco de mer seed.
African countries by population.Mauritius: The only home of the dodo, which was extinct by the late 1600s.
African countries by population.Botswana: It has more than 100,000 elephants, among the largest populations anywhere, and the Okavango Delta.
African countries by population.Libya: It has Africa's largest proven oil reserves, and most people live along the Mediterranean coast.
African countries by population.Senegal: Dakar, its capital, is the westernmost city on mainland Africa.
African countries by population.Morocco: The Fez el-Bali medina is one of the world's largest car-free urban areas.
African countries by population.Kenya: Its Great Rift Valley and marathon runners are famous, and the Great Migration crosses the Maasai Mara.
African countries by population.South Africa: It has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
African countries by population.Egypt: Most Egyptians live along the Nile, on a small fraction of the country's land.
African countries by population.Nigeria: Africa's most populous country has hundreds of ethnic groups, and its film industry Nollywood is among the world's largest.

Impact craters by size.Kaali, Estonia: This small crater in Saaremaa island is the best-known meteorite crater in Europe, and it may have inspired local myths about a fallen sun.
Impact craters by size.Wolfe Creek, Australia: Also called Kandimalal, this crater in Western Australia is a well-preserved meteorite crater and sacred to the local Aboriginal people.
Impact craters by size.Meteor Crater, Arizona: Also called Barringer Crater, it was the first crater proven to be from an impact, thanks to Daniel Barringer's work in the early 1900s.
Impact craters by size.Lonar Lake, India: This lake in Maharashtra fills a crater in basaltic rock, and its unusually salty, alkaline water holds rare microbes.
Impact craters by size.Lake Bosumtwi, Ghana: This lake in Ghana fills a crater about one million years old; local Ashanti people regard it as sacred and a home of the god Twi.
Impact craters by size.Ries, Germany: The Nördlinger Ries holds a town, Nördlingen, whose old buildings contain millions of tiny impact diamonds in their stone.
Impact craters by size.Popigai, Russia: Popigai holds one of the world's largest known deposits of impact diamonds, formed when the asteroid struck graphite-bearing rock about 35 million years ago.
Impact craters by size.Sudbury, Canada: Sudbury is rich in nickel and other metals and is among the largest known impact structures; one theory says metals arrived with the impactor.
Impact craters by size.Chicxulub, Mexico: The crater is linked to the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs about 66 million years ago, and its rim runs under the Yucatan town of Mérida region.
Impact craters by size.Vredefort, South Africa: Vredefort is the largest verified impact structure on Earth, about two billion years old, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The universe's first moments, in order.Planck epoch ends: The Planck epoch is a time when the known laws of physics break down, and gravity may have been unified with other forces.
The universe's first moments, in order.Cosmic inflation ends: Inflation expanded space by an enormous factor in a fraction of a second, smoothing the universe and seeding future galaxies.
The universe's first moments, in order.Electroweak force splits: At this point the weak force and electromagnetism separated, which is why particles gained mass through the Higgs field.
The universe's first moments, in order.Protons and neutrons form: The universe cooled enough for quarks to combine into protons and neutrons, the building blocks of every atom.
The universe's first moments, in order.Neutrinos decouple: Neutrinos stopped interacting and began streaming freely, forming a cosmic background that still fills space today.
The universe's first moments, in order.First nuclei form: In the first few minutes, protons and neutrons fused into hydrogen, helium and lithium nuclei, creating most of the universe's helium.
The universe's first moments, in order.Light breaks free (CMB): Atoms formed and light could finally travel freely, a glow we can still detect as the cosmic microwave background.
The universe's first moments, in order.First stars ignite: These first stars lit up the cosmic dark ages and made the first heavy elements; they were likely huge and short-lived.
The universe's first moments, in order.The Sun forms: Our Sun formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust, about 4.6 billion years ago, long after the Big Bang.
The universe's first moments, in order.Today: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old, and space is still expanding, at an accelerating rate.

Amazon through the years.Amazon.com opens: Jeff Bezos started the company from his garage in the Seattle area, selling only books at first.
Amazon through the years.Amazon Prime: The membership launched with free two-day shipping for $79 a year, and it has since grown into video and music, too.
Amazon through the years.Amazon Web Services S3: The first of the services launched as AWS, which now earns most of the company's profit.
Amazon through the years.Amazon buys Audible: The audiobook company cost a reported $300 million and later formed the backbone of Amazon's audio push.
Amazon through the years.Kindle Fire: The tablet, priced at $199, was Amazon's first tablet, arriving four years after the original Kindle e-reader.
Amazon through the years.Amazon buys Twitch: The livestreaming platform, bought for around $970 million, grew out of the site Justin.tv.
Amazon through the years.First Prime Day: Its first edition was held in July 2015 to celebrate Amazon's twentieth anniversary.
Amazon through the years.Amazon buys Whole Foods: It cost about $13.7 billion, the company's largest acquisition until then, and put it in physical groceries.
Amazon through the years.Amazon Go store opens: The cashier-free store used cameras and sensors so shoppers could simply walk out with their goods.
Amazon through the years.Amazon buys MGM: The $8.45 billion deal brought the studio behind James Bond and Rocky to the company.

Home video game consoles by first releas.Atari 2600: This cartridge-based console brought arcade-style games home, and games included Pitfall and Space Invaders.
Home video game consoles by first releas.NES (Famicom): The Famicom launched in Japan in 1983, and the NES revived the US game business after the 1983 crash.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Sega Mega Drive / Genesis: Sega's 16-bit rival to Nintendo, which arrived in the US in 1989, was home to Sonic.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Super Nintendo: Called the Super Famicom in Japan, it was the home of Super Mario World.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Nintendo 64: It was one of the first with an analogue stick, and has four controller ports.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Sega Dreamcast: Sega's last console had a built-in modem and online play, but it was discontinued in 2001.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Original Xbox: Microsoft's first console, with a hard drive, made Halo a hit.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Xbox 360: It popularised online console play and was famous for its 'red ring of death' hardware fault.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Nintendo Wii: Motion controls helped it sell over 100 million, and it drew non-gamers to gaming.
Home video game consoles by first releas.Wii U: Its GamePad had a built-in touchscreen, but the console sold only around 13 million.

Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Hyksos: Foreign rulers from the Levant who held the Nile Delta; they brought horse-drawn chariots and the composite bow to Egypt.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Kushites: Kings from Nubia formed Egypt's 25th Dynasty, and they revived pyramid building, raising small steep ones at Nuri and El-Kurru.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Assyrians: Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671 BC, but Assyrian control proved short, ending within about a decade under Psamtik I.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Persians: Cambyses II won at Pelusium; later sources claim he drove cats and other sacred animals before his troops so Egyptians would not shoot.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Macedonians: Alexander took Egypt in 332 BC almost without a fight and founded Alexandria, soon the great city of the Mediterranean.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Romans: After Antony and Cleopatra died, Egypt became Augustus's personal province, and its grain fed the city of Rome.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Arabs: Amr ibn al-As conquered Egypt, then founded Fustat, the garrison town whose site later became part of Cairo.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Fatimids: This dynasty founded Cairo in 969 and set up Al-Azhar around 970, among the oldest universities still operating.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Ayyubids: Founded by Saladin, famed for retaking Jerusalem in 1187, this dynasty also began the great Citadel overlooking Cairo.
Who ruled Egypt: when each took control.Mamluks: A dynasty of former slave-soldiers; they beat the Mongols at Ain Jalut in 1260, halting the Mongol advance toward Africa.

Metric prefixes by size.pico-: From Italian 'piccolo', 'small'; in one picosecond, light travels only about 0.3 millimetres.
Metric prefixes by size.nano-: From Greek for 'dwarf'; your fingernails grow roughly one nanometre per second.
Metric prefixes by size.micro-: From Greek for 'small'; a red blood cell is roughly 7 micrometres across.
Metric prefixes by size.milli-: Latin for a thousand, yet most millipedes have far fewer than a thousand legs.
Metric prefixes by size.centi-: Latin for a hundred; the Celsius scale, once called centigrade, borrowed from this idea.
Metric prefixes by size.kilo-: From Greek for a thousand, the kilogram was once a platinum cylinder kept near Paris, until 2019.
Metric prefixes by size.mega-: From Greek for 'great'; a megapixel image holds about a million dots.
Metric prefixes by size.giga-: From Greek for 'giant', and a gigabyte is a billion bytes.
Metric prefixes by size.tera-: From Greek for 'monster', and the first terabyte drives were extremely expensive.
Metric prefixes by size.peta-: Its name comes from the Greek for five, since it equals 1,000 to the fifth power, with a letter dropped.

When these game controllers and add-ons.Atari 2600 joystick: The Atari 2600 joystick had one button and one stick, and its simple design shaped how gamers held controllers for decades.
When these game controllers and add-ons.R.O.B. the robot: R.O.B. was a toy robot that Nintendo used to sell its console to US retailers, who were wary of video games after the 1983 crash.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Power Glove: The Power Glove was a Nintendo accessory that flopped, but it was widely used by hobbyists and appeared in the film The Wizard.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Rumble Pak: The Rumble Pak plugged into the Nintendo 64 controller and made it vibrate, starting force feedback in mainstream gaming.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Game Boy Camera: The Game Boy Camera could take tiny black and white photos with 128 by 112 pixels and was named the smallest digital camera by Guinness.
When these game controllers and add-ons.EyeToy: EyeToy was a USB camera for the PlayStation 2 that let players control games with body movements.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Wii Remote: The Wii Remote used motion sensing to control games, and it brought in a wide audience of casual players.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Kinect: Kinect let Xbox 360 players control games with their bodies and voices, and it set a Guinness record as the fastest-selling consumer device.
When these game controllers and add-ons.PlayStation VR: PlayStation VR brought console virtual reality to many homes, and it was a headset for the PS4.
When these game controllers and add-ons.Joy-Con: Joy-Con controllers can be detached from the Nintendo Switch and used as two small controllers, one in each hand.

Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Carrie: King's first published novel. He reportedly threw the draft away and his wife Tabitha fished it from the trash.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Christine: Based on a book about a haunted 1958 Plymouth Fury, directed by horror master John Carpenter.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Stand by Me: Based on the novella 'The Body'. Rob Reiner directed, and River Phoenix gave a standout performance.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Pet Sematary (original): King wrote it after a close call: his young son ran toward a road. The film's director was Mary Lambert.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Misery: Kathy Bates won the Best Actress Oscar for playing Annie Wilkes, the 'number one fan'.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.The Shawshank Redemption: Based on a novella, it flopped at the box office before becoming a beloved classic on home video.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.The Green Mile: The book was published in six monthly instalments in 1996.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.The Mist: Frank Darabont's ending is far bleaker than the novella's, and King said he loved it.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.It (Skarsgård): Bill Skarsgård played Pennywise. At the time, it became the highest-grossing horror film ever.
Stephen King movie adaptations by releas.Doctor Sleep: The sequel to The Shining adapts King's 2013 novel and recreates Kubrick's hotel.

Beloved children's books, by publication.Little Women: Louisa May Alcott based the March sisters on her own family. Jo, the writer, is widely seen as her portrait of herself.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Heidi: Johanna Spyri's tale of an orphan in the Swiss Alps has been translated into dozens of languages. It made her a world-famous author.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Anne of Green Gables: Lucy Maud Montgomery's red-haired orphan lives on Prince Edward Island. She insisted her name was spelled "with an e."
Beloved children's books, by publication.The Secret Garden: Frances Hodgson Burnett's tale is set in Yorkshire, where a lonely girl finds a locked garden. The story also deals with healing.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Little House in the Big Woods: Laura Ingalls Wilder wrote her first book at 65, based on her frontier childhood in Wisconsin. It started the Little House series.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Mary Poppins: P. L. Travers' nanny is far sterner than Julie Andrews' sweet screen version. Travers was an Australian-born writer who disliked the film.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Pippi Longstocking: Astrid Lindgren made up stories for her sick daughter, who asked for a tale about Pippi Longstocking. The super-strong girl lives alone with a horse.
Beloved children's books, by publication.The Borrowers: Mary Norton's story is about tiny people who live in the walls and "borrow" household objects. It won the Carnegie Medal.
Beloved children's books, by publication.The Phantom Tollbooth: Norton Juster wrote it while avoiding another project, and Jules Feiffer illustrated it. Milo's journey is full of wordplay and puns.
Beloved children's books, by publication.Holes: Louis Sachar's tale about a boys' detention camp in the desert won the Newbery Medal. Sachar also wrote the screenplay.

How many basic signs in each writing sys.Rotokas alphabet: Used on Bougainville in Papua New Guinea, it is among the smallest alphabets in the world, with just twelve letters.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Younger Futhark runes: Used in Viking Age Scandinavia, it trimmed the older 24 runes to 16, so each rune had to stand for several sounds.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Ogham (original set): Carved along the edge of standing stones in early medieval Ireland, its letters are strokes cut across a central line.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Phoenician alphabet: It has only consonants, yet it is the ancestor of the Greek, Latin and Hebrew alphabets.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Elder Futhark runes: The name comes from its first six runes, f-u-th-a-r-k; the oldest inscriptions date to around the 2nd century.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Georgian alphabet: Georgia's script has no capital letters, and its look is unlike any other writing system in the world.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Thai consonants: Thai has 44 consonant letters but only about 21 consonant sounds, because several letters share the same sound.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Hiragana (basic): Developed from cursive Chinese characters, it was used mostly by court women in Heian Japan.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Cherokee syllabary: Sequoyah, who could not read, invented it in the 1820s, and literacy spread across the Cherokee Nation within a few years.
How many basic signs in each writing sys.Jōyō kanji: Japan's official list of 2,136 characters for everyday use was set in 2010, though educated readers know more.

US mattress sizes by width.Crib: Under US safety rules, it must fit snugly, because gaps wider than two fingers can trap a baby.
US mattress sizes by width.Twin: Common in dorm rooms, it measures 38 by 75 inches, with a longer 'Twin XL' version at 80 inches.
US mattress sizes by width.Full: Two adults sharing it get just 27 inches each, about the width of a crib mattress.
US mattress sizes by width.Queen: The most popular size in America at 60 by 80 inches.
US mattress sizes by width.Olympic queen: It is slightly wider than a queen at 66 inches, and sheets are harder to find.
US mattress sizes by width.California king: Narrower but longer than a standard king, at 72 by 84 inches, suiting tall sleepers.
US mattress sizes by width.King: At 76 inches wide, it is exactly the width of two Twin XL mattresses side by side.
US mattress sizes by width.Texas king: Roughly 80 by 98 inches, this niche size usually needs custom sheets.
US mattress sizes by width.Wyoming king: It is a perfect square, 84 inches on each side.
US mattress sizes by width.Alaskan king: At 108 by 108 inches, nine feet on a side, it could sleep a family.

Marsupials by weight.Honey possum: A tiny Australian marsupial that lives on nectar and pollen. It has a long, brush-tipped tongue and is the only mammal that feeds entirely on flowers.
Marsupials by weight.Sugar glider: Flaps of skin between its front and back legs let it glide through the air for a distance of 45 metres or more. It eats sap, nectar and insects.
Marsupials by weight.Numbat: A striped Australian marsupial that eats termites, up to 20,000 in a day. It is the emblem of Western Australia, and is endangered.
Marsupials by weight.Bilby: This long-eared desert marsupial digs burrows and is Australia's Easter icon, as a chocolate version replaces the Easter bunny, which is a pest in Australia.
Marsupials by weight.Virginia opossum: North America's only marsupial. When frightened, it may fall into a stupor that looks like death. It can have more than a dozen joeys in a litter.
Marsupials by weight.Tasmanian devil: Named for its screeches, this Tasmanian carnivore has one of the strongest bites for its size. It has been hit by a contagious facial cancer.
Marsupials by weight.Red-necked wallaby: Native to eastern Australia and Tasmania, it is also a feral colony in parts of Britain. Like all kangaroo relatives, it moves by hopping.
Marsupials by weight.Wombat: The wombat's pouch faces backward so that it doesn't fill with soil when digging. It can run at about 40 km/h in short bursts.
Marsupials by weight.Red kangaroo: The largest marsupial alive, with males that can stand taller than a person. A baby is born the size of a jellybean and crawls into the pouch.
Marsupials by weight.Diprotodon (extinct): The largest marsupial ever, as big as a rhinoceros, it roamed Australia until about 40,000 years ago. Its name means two forward teeth.

Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Leave seed potatoes to sprout: Seed potatoes are small tubers set in light to grow short, sturdy shoots called chits. This is called chitting, and it gives plants a head start.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Plant them in a trench: Potatoes are grown from pieces of potato, not seeds. Each tuber is planted so that the eyes face up in a trench, about 10 cm deep.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Shoots poke up: The first green shoots appear a few weeks after planting. A late frost can kill the tender leaves, so growers cover them if it is cold.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Pile soil around the shoots: Earthing up buries the stems and stops the new tubers going green from sunlight. Green potatoes contain solanine and are bitter and toxic.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Flowers appear: Potato plants flower white, pink or purple, and may form small green berries that are poisonous. The plant is related to tomatoes and deadly nightshade.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Leaves turn yellow: As the plant dies back, the tubers stop growing and the skins toughen. This is the signal that the main crop is ready to dig.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Dig up the potatoes: Digging potatoes is like finding buried treasure, and new potatoes are often dug early. Potatoes originated in the Andes, and were brought to Europe in the 1500s.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Wash off the soil: Washed potatoes are best used soon, since unwashed ones store better in the dark. Light and cold change their taste, and damage the tubers.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Cut into chips: In Britain chips are thick-cut fried potatoes, and in the US they are called fries. Belgium claims to have invented them, in the 1600s.
Growing potatoes, from tuber to chips.Fry until golden: Double frying, first at low heat and then hot, makes chips crispy outside and fluffy inside. The golden colour comes from the Maillard reaction.

Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Mother packs a basket: In Perrault's 1697 version she carries cakes and butter; the Brothers Grimm's Little Red Cap has cake and wine for the sick grandmother.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Sets off through the woods: The woods are the classic fairy-tale place of danger, and the story's warning about leaving the path is its central moral.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Meets the wolf on the path: Perrault's 1697 version ends grimly: the wolf eats her, and a moral warns girls about charming strangers.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Picks flowers along the way: In the Grimms' version the wolf suggests the flowers himself, as a way to distract her while he rushes ahead.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Wolf reaches Grandma first: The oldest oral versions, like the French Story of Grandmother, let the girl outwit the wolf and escape by herself.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Wolf swallows Grandma: Being swallowed whole and surviving is an ancient folktale motif, shared with Jonah and the great fish.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Wolf climbs into her bed: The Brothers Grimm published their version in 1812, calling the heroine Rotkäppchen, or Little Red Cap.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.\"What big eyes you have!\": The back-and-forth about big eyes, ears and teeth is the most famous dialogue in the story and builds to the wolf's reveal.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Wolf gobbles up Red: In the Grimm telling, Red and her grandmother come out alive after the wolf is cut open, an ending Perrault's version never gave.
Little Red Riding Hood, in story order.Woodcutter comes to the rescue: The woodcutter, a huntsman in the Grimm version, was added to give the tale its rescue; Perrault's version had no happy ending.

The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Rosh Hashanah: The Jewish new year is marked by blowing the shofar and dipping apples in honey for a sweet year ahead.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Yom Kippur: The Day of Atonement involves a fast of about 25 hours; in Israel the roads empty and children ride bicycles down the highways.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Sukkot: Families eat in a temporary hut, a sukkah, roofed with branches so the stars show through, recalling the desert wanderings.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Hanukkah: The story of the oil lasting eight days first appears in the Talmud, centuries after the Maccabees' victory it commemorates.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Tu BiShvat: Called the new year for trees, it is marked by eating fruits like figs, dates and almonds, and by planting trees in Israel.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Purim: People read the Book of Esther, dress in costumes, send gifts of food and eat triangular hamantaschen.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Passover: The seder retells the Exodus with four cups of wine, and the youngest child asks the Four Questions.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Lag BaOmer: Bonfires light up Israel on this day, which remembers Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and a pause in the mourning of the Omer.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Shavuot: Marking the giving of the Torah at Sinai, it is traditional to stay up all night studying and to eat dairy foods like cheesecake.
The Jewish year, from Rosh Hashanah.Tisha B'Av: A fast mourning the destruction of both Temples, which tradition says fell on the same date, it is regarded as the saddest day of the Jewish calendar.
